item.title: Curative-intent management of de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma: an evidence-based consensus guideline from the International Collaborating Oncology Organisations.
item.author: Guo QJ, Liu Q, Bossi P, Bonomo P, Colevas AD, Lee NY, Lu TZ, Lee V, Mehanna H, Ng WT, O'Sullivan B, Psyrri A, Rühle A, Szturz P, Thariat J, AlHussain H, Ahn YC, Bernsdorf M, Chan AW, Chan A, Chan ATC, Chow JCH, Corry J, Chua MLK, Chen MY, Chen NY, Chen XZ, Grégoire V, Harrington KJ, Hu CS, Han YQ, Huang S, Jin F, Langendijk JA, Li JG, Lin JC, Lang JY, Le QT, Lin SJ, Lau TTS, Mai HQ, Ma J, Moon SH, Ozyar E, Qu S, Rosenthal DI, Tao YG, Tahara M, Tin W, Wee J, Wang RS, Wang Y, Wong CE, Ying HM, Yi JL, Zhang L, Fan DM, Yom SS, Lee AWM.
item.description:
Patients with de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma were historically deemed incurable and treated with palliative intent. Emergence of potent systemic therapy in combination with local treatment for both locoregional and metastatic diseases has enabled long-term survival in some patients. This international guideline was developed through consensus-building by 54 experts from 46 centres across 18 countries or regions and endorsed by 17 oncology organisations. 32 recommendations across seven clinical domains were formulated, including 29 strong (≥80% agreement [consensus] or high quality of evidence) and three conditional recommendations (67-79% agreement). item.title: Development of the Children's Oncology Group long-term follow-up guideline for cancer genetics evaluation in childhood cancer survivors.
item.author: Janardan SK, Devine A, Grieve LM, Seibel E, Villani A, Porter CC, Diller LR, Gramatges MM, Constine LS, Landier W, Bhatia S, Hudson MM, Ehrhardt MJ, Friedman DN, Turcotte LM, Nichols KE.
item.description:
Up to 12% of childhood cancer survivors have an underlying cancer predisposition syndrome (CPS). As a result, these childhood cancer survivors are at increased risk for developing and succumbing to subsequent malignant neoplasms. Identifying childhood cancer survivors with CPS is essential to improving overall outcomes by informing tailored approaches to cancer screening, treatment, and, for some, risk-reducing interventions. Despite these potential benefits, it is often unclear which childhood cancer survivors warrant referral for genetic counselling and germline genetic testing. item.title: Zamtocabtagene autoleucel, a tandem CD20-CD19-directed CAR T-cell therapy, for second line treatment of large B-cell lymphoma in patients ineligible for transplantation (DALY 2-EU): primary analysis of an open-label, multicentre, randomised phase 2 study.
item.author: Borchmann P, van Meerten T, Iacoboni G, Bories P, Dreger P, Mutsaers P, Gopcsa L, Edinger M, Gergely L, von Tresckow B, Neumeister P, Steiner N, Jäger U, Moreno AT, Griškevičius L, Lemonnier F, van Doesum J, Kersten MJ, Rudzki JD, Shah NN, Orentas R, Friedrichs B, Miltenyi S, Overstijns T, Bürger I, Zadoyan G, Brillant C, Paul P, van Heteren P, Holtkamp S, Vandenberghe P.
item.description:
Background Anti-CD19 CAR T-cell therapy is the standard second-line treatment for patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma. However, there is no evidence from randomised controlled trials in patients ineligible for transplantation. To address this gap, we compared zamtocabtagene autoleucel (zamto-cel), a CAR T-cell therapy directed at CD20 and CD19, with rituximab-gemcitabine-oxaliplatin (R-GemOx) chemoimmunotherapy in patients ineligible for transplantation with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma. Methods DALY 2-EU is an open-label, multicentre, randomised, phase 2 trial conducted at 45 centres across 12 countries in Europe. item.title: Assessment of comprehensiveness of national cancer control plans using a multiagent artificial intelligence model: a global analysis.
item.author: Kumar CJ, Reddy CL, Pearson H, Atun R, Global Cancer Control Policy Research Group.
item.description:
Background National cancer control plans (NCCPs) vary in scope and comprehensiveness, yet expert-led review is resource intensive and limits cross-country comparability. We aimed to assess NCCP comprehensiveness across 50 countries using the policy reasoning integrated sequential model (PRISM), a validated multiagent artificial intelligence (AI) system. Methods We identified the most recent national NCCP for each country from the International Cancer Control Partnership repository, the WHO Noncommunicable Disease Document Repository, and government websites; sub-national plans, broader non-communicable disease or health-sector strategies, drafts, and superseded versions were excluded.
